Maintenance Procedure Information System
 | Protection | Maintenance Procedures
Document No.: OCR-084-r0a | Equipment:
 Overcurrent and Earth Leakage Protection, SC
 Sepam 2000
 Schneider Electric MERLIN GERIN
Issued to: 
 Distribution Companies
Status: 
 Draft
Approval date: 
 2009 | Procedure:
 Three-phase secondary injection device (voltage and current)
Next review date: 
 2014
Introduction
System Feeder Protection Management Numerical. This document sets out the steps for testing and calibrating the directional and non-directional overcurrent and earth leakage protection device. This device is installed in the incoming cells of the medium voltage distributor, in addition to the measuring functions (active and reactive power, current, voltage, power factor and frequency).
This document was prepared by Canal Electricity Distribution Company and was reviewed and approved by the MPIS coordinators.
Safety Precautions
Issue an approved work order with all items completed. | 
Maintenance and test personnel must carry the occupational safety and health category card. | 
Switch off the circuit breaker and withdraw it outside the cell (place the circuit breaker in the test position). | 
Ensure warning signs are posted on the cells to be worked on. | 
Occupational safety and health instructions must be followed at the work site. | 
Ensure the correct phase sequence of voltage and current on the protection device VRIR - VSIS - VTIT using the Power Analyzer before switching off. | 
Do not open current transformer terminals while in service or under test. | 
Observe polarity when dealing with DC voltage. | 
Ensure the protection device is earthed in the cell. | 
Tools, Instruments and Equipment Used
Three Phase Circuit Analyzer device. | 
Three-phase secondary injection device (voltage and current). | 
Load clamp and avometer. | 
Suitable laptop computer with the relay software. | 
Procedures to be Carried Out
First: Overcurrent Test, Non-Directional (measured values are compared with rated values)
Ensure the DC auxiliary voltage is present on the protection device at points 1A 3 (+), 1A 4 (-) — Figure 4 | 1.
Prepare the injection device and supply it with the appropriate AC auxiliary voltage for operation | 2.
Connect the current leads to the protection device at points 2B 1, 2B 2 | 3.
Raise the current gradually until reaching the pickup current IPICK UP of the protection device and record this value | 4.
Lower the current gradually until reaching the IReset current of the protection device and record this value | 5.
Calculate the reset factor K Reset Factor = I PICK UP / I RESET > 95% | 6.
Repeat these steps for the second and third phases | 7.
Connect the TRIP leads of the device to the Stop Timer terminals of the injection device to calculate the tripping time | 8.
Second: Earth Leakage Test, Non-Directional
Connect the current leads to the protection device at points 2A 3, 2A 4 | 1.
Raise the current gradually until reaching the pickup current I Pick up of the protection device and record this value | 2.
Lower the current gradually until reaching the I Reset current of the protection device and record this value | 3.
Calculate the reset factor K Reset Factor = I RESET / I PICK UP < 95% | 4.
Connect the TRIP leads of the device to the Stop Timer terminals of the injection device to calculate the tripping time | 5.
Third: Directional Overcurrent Test
Set the SEPAM 2000 device to suitable setting values, e.g. (I = 0–1 In, t = 100 ms), (angle = 0–90), noting that the load angle is set in the first quadrant only for the device
Fourth: Testing the Directional Earth Leakage Characteristic
Set the SEPAM 2000 protection device to suitable setting values (I = 0 : 0.2 In) (t = 100 ms) (angle = 0 : -45), noting that the angle between (VN & IN) can only be set on the device in the fourth quadrant (zero to -90) | 1.
Connect the secondary injection device to the voltage and current windings, observing the polarity of the windings: current leads at points (3 - 4) 2A; voltage leads at points (7 - 8) 4A | 2.
Operate the injection device and inject suitable current and voltage for the setting values | 3.
Connect the Trip leads of the protection device to the Stop timer of the secondary injection device | 4.
Change the load angle between current and voltage on the injection device from zero to 360 to find that the protection device operates Trip in the range from (-85) to (+85), where the angle is the directionality angle set on the protection device, which is in the first quadrant, and Trip does not operate in the rest of the range | 5.
Fifth: How to Set the Directionality of the Directional Protection Device In Situ
After finishing the test of the directional overcurrent and earth leakage protection element in items three and four, all the test unit leads shall be disconnected from the device and a Simulation of overcurrent and earth leakage shall be carried out as follows:
Directional Overcurrent
Set the device directionality to Reverse mode as shown in the drawing | 1.
Connect the two cables in parallel and load them with the normal load in the distributor, determining the direction of the Load Flow | 2.
Isolate the tripping terminal of the directional overcurrent for cable No. (1) | 3.
Lower the directional overcurrent setting value to a value below the cell value; in this case the device does not give a tripping signal | 4.
Reverse the device directionality in item (1) to Forward | 5.
Repeat what happened in item (4) until pickup of the device occurs and a tripping signal is given | 6.
Reset the directionality to Reverse mode, set the device to the normal setting, and connect the tripping terminals to the protection device | 7.
Repeat items (1:7) on cable No. (2) | 8.
Directional Earth Leakage
Set the device directionality to Reverse mode | 1.
Disconnect phase R from the voltage on the protection device | 2.
Ensure the directionality is tested by two methods, namely: | 3.
First Method
Make a bridge across phases S, T; current of phase R then passes through the earth leakage winding of the protection device and directional earth leakage pickup occurs. In this case, if the device gives a tripping signal, reverse the directionality and repeat the test until pickup of the device occurs and only a pickup signal is given, without a tripping signal | 1.
Second Method
Make a bridge across phase R current with earth; current then passes through the earth leakage winding as the sum of S and T, and pickup is opposite to the direction of R current; directional earth leakage pickup thus occurs and a tripping signal is given | 1.
To ensure the directionality is correct, make a bridge across phase S current with earth; in this case pickup of the device occurs but no tripping signal is given, and repeat likewise with phase T current | 2.
Connect the R-phase voltage and remove the short-circuit from phases S, T as well as phases R, N, with the protection devices set to the normal setting of the devices | 3.
